focus: The sk-git/026 regression: who moved the worktrees back and where the reaper's daemon handling went
noveltyJustification: Nine of ten findings are new to the packet: the deletion commit, the MCP-versus-fsmonitor family correction, the wrapper config write-back, and the live census were all unrecorded.
keyQuestions: Q1. What unset speckit.worktreeBase and removed the reaper's daemon handling, and does anything still create worktrees under .worktrees/ by default?
Q2. What is git 2.50.1's documented fsmonitor daemon lifecycle on macOS, and how do fsmonitor.socketDir, idle shutdown and git fsmonitor--daemon stop behave when the daemon is wedged?
Q3. Is event overload the real cause of the hang, or is there a known daemon deadlock in this git version, for example around --ipc-threads or the cookie-file handshake?
Q4. Which call sites in the repo's hooks and scripts run git without a timeout, and which of them should opt out of fsmonitor?
Q5. What is the safest default: fsmonitor on with worktrees outside the checkout, or fsmonitor off for the main checkout and on per worktree?
answeredQuestions: Q1. What unset speckit.worktreeBase and removed the reaper's daemon handling, and does anything still create worktrees under .worktrees/ by default?

A repo commit reverted the relocated worktree base
The unset is recoverable from this shell's history

graphEvents.label: What unset the worktree base and removed the reaper daemon handling
Reaper daemon block deleted by commit 3c7c3f83874
Removed logic targeted MCP context-server daemons, never git fsmonitor
Launch wrapper writes speckit.worktreeBase back on every unset launch

label: Commit 3c7c3f83874 (2026-09-03) deleted the reaper's --reap-daemons flag, the _daemon_worktree_path_from_cmdline and _daemon_cmdline_is_orphan helpers, and the whole ORPHAN DAEMON REPORTING block from .opencode/bin/worktree-reaper.sh.

The deleted reaper logic only enumerated pgrep -f context-server.js and skipped any command line not matching *node*context-server.js*, so it targeted retired spec-memory MCP daemons and never matched git fsmonitor--daemon.
Restoring the reaper's daemon handling would not stop a single fsmonitor daemon; a fsmonitor reaper is new work rather than a revert.
speckit.worktreeBase is unversioned local config: no commit can unset it, and this checkout currently has no such key set, so the relocation policy record simply is not in the repository.

.skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh:292-295 writes speckit.worktreeBase whenever the key is unset, and _wn_base_dir() defaults to <toplevel>/.worktrees, so one launch without SPECKIT_WORKTREE_BASE re-pins the in-checkout base permanently.

The auto-pin arrived in f83952c3a94 (2026-09-11), three weeks after a69a621a39a (2026-08-21) introduced the configurable base, opening a window where a launch re-pinned .worktrees with no operator intent.
The in-checkout default is still documented as the default in worktree-naming.sh:13 and README.md:115,125, and the changelog advertises unsetting the config as the supported way back to .worktrees.
Live state matches the in-checkout default: no speckit.worktreeBase, an empty ~/worktrees, and 13 worktrees under Public/.worktrees (087, 103, 140, 144, 145, 156, 197, 216, 217, 218, 219, 230, 231).

Eleven git fsmonitor--daemon run --detach --ipc-threads=8 processes were alive at 09:22Z, the oldest from Oct 11 18:29:55 (PID 1157), all from Xcode git-core, and nothing in the repo starts, bounds or stops them.
worktree-reaper.sh is a manual CLI whose published invariant is now never signals a process, so daemon killing must move to a separate entry point instead of being re-added to it.
